projects.title: [开源推荐] Agent Usage：在本地统计 AI 编程工具用量与费用的桌面应用
projects.author: hongshuo-wang

github.name: hongshuo-wang/agent-usage-desktop
github.description: A desktop app for local usage, cost, throughput, and session analytics across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and OpenClaw. | 在本地统一统计和分析 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 与 OpenClaw 的用量、费用、吞吐和会话。

projects.summary: Agent Usage 是一款免费开源的桌面应用，读取本机 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 和 OpenClaw 的用量记录，集中展示 Token 消耗、估算费用和使用趋势。可以按时间、来源、模型和项目筛选，也能回查 Claude Code 与 Codex 的会话时间线、工具调用和错误。适合同时使用多个 AI 编程工具、想了解用量分布的用户。无需注册账号，会话内容保存在本机。 亮点 将多个 AI 编程工具的记录放在同一个界面中，方便比较模型和项目的 Token 用量、估算费用与本机观测吞吐。 统计与会话回溯联动：从用量筛选进入对应会话，查看事件时间线、工具调用和错误；深度会话回溯目前支持 Claude Code 与 Codex。 直接读取已有本地记录，增量扫描并自动去重，不需要修改 Agent 的使用方式，也不会上传会话内容。 使用历史定价快照，后续价格目录更新不会静默改写已有费用；显示的是本地估算费用，不是服务商账单。 提供中英文界面、深浅色主题、系统托盘及会话内容保留期与清理设置。项目采用 Go、Tauri、React 和 SQLite，使用 Apache-2.0 许可证。 截图或演示视频 补充说明 这是作者自荐项目。 中文介绍： 下载安装：

projects.title: AUDR by Chargebee
projects.summary: AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record) is an open standard, for capturing who initiated an agent run and what it cost across every system that run touches. Inspired by the telecom industry's Call Detail Record, AUDR defines a common JSON schema that any harness, router, or billing system can emit and ingest. Three core rules make it work: a shared run ID minted by the harness, clear field ownership, and strict merge rules where conflicts are rejected and corrections are new records.

projects.title: Push Agent
projects.summary: Push Agent lets visitors subscribe to browser notifications with one click, then reach them on Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, even when your site is closed. Unlike most push tools it uses standard Web Push: no Firebase, unlimited notifications on every plan and simple monthly prices. Free WordPress and Joomla plugins, or one line of code for any site. Schedule, target by country or device, A/B test titles, auto-send new posts by RSS, and send WooCommerce order updates.

projects.title: Kaya, AI Coding Terminal

Use @mentions to coordinate tasks, monitor agent activity, and catch work that drifts off course. Code remotely through Feishu, Slack, or Web Remote Access. Available on macOS and Windows, with a free plan and a 7-day trial.

projects.title: Show HN: OpenChart – OSS TradingView alternative with your own AI agent
projects.author: Warren93

github.name: longsurf-ai/openchart
github.description: Trade with charts, alerts, scripts, and your AI agents.

projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Weilun, cofounder of OpenChart. We built OpenChart because we wanted Claude and Codex to interface with the markets, like most of humans do, through charts rather than through CLIs. With your existing AI plans, your agent can work directly with your charts: annotate a setup, write an indicator, investigate a market move, or create an alert. The chart, conversation, and research live in the same workspace. OpenChart alerts on any market move: draw any shape on a chart and attach an alert. When price crosses it, the alert triggers your agent to investigate the move and save the research in your workspace. The agents can work with charts, indicators, and alerts. Custom indicators and alert conditions are written in [Tea]( https://github.com/longsurf-ai/tea ), a programming language we built for the markets. We believe software shouldn’t impose artificial friction on your workflow. OpenChart is built on that belief with no software cap. The source code is publicly available, and you can use free market data from day one. We also offer optional paid cloud market data for lower latency. Everything is private. Your charts, research, and indicator code are stored on your own computer, with the app's backend running locally too. We currently support only macOS on Apple Silicon, but we're expanding to more platforms. Website: https://openchart.co/ Download: https://downloads.longsurf.ai/openchart/darwin/arm64/OpenCha... We built OpenChart because we want to explore how assets can be co-manages by agents and humans. I'd especially like to hear how you are using agents to help with your investment journey. If you like what we're building, a star on GitHub would mean a lot to us: https://github.com/longsurf-ai/openchart

projects.title: RDesk
projects.summary: RDesk lets IT help desks see and control a Windows PC or Android phone straight from the browser — nothing to install for the technician. The person at the computer always clicks Allow, file access is a separate Allow, and a visible banner shows who is connected with an End button. Unattended access is opt-in and password-protected. Multi-tenant team accounts, per-user agent books, session history and self-hosting.

projects.title: Muxly
projects.summary: Muxly is a native tmux client for iPhone and iPad. Run Claude Code, Codex or any long job inside tmux on your server, close the app, and it keeps running. When you come back, Muxly reattaches: tmux windows become native tabs and panes are one tap away. Optional end-to-end encrypted bell notifications tell you when an agent finishes or needs input. Direct SSH to your own servers, no Muxly account. SFTP, a file editor, port forwarding, hardware keyboard support and much more.

projects.title: 做了个查 AI 用量的 App
projects.author: chenzhe
projects.summary: 做了个 App 叫 **usAge**：连上账号，用了多少、什么时候重置、还剩多少钱，一屏看清；放个小组件在桌面，抬头就能看到。 ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/posts/v2ex/cover.jpg) ## 支持哪些服务 Claude 、Codex 、Cursor 、智谱 GLM / Z.ai 、Kimi 、MiniMax 、Xiaomi MiMo 、Qoder 、OpenRouter 、DeepSeek （鸿蒙版的 Qoder 在下个版本）。 - 订阅制看已用比例和重置倒计时，按量付费看余额和花销 - 网页登录或者填 API Key 都能连 - 没有你在用的？ App 里可以申请接入，直接回帖也行 ## 主要功能 - **一屏看全部额度**：5 小时窗口、每周额度、Token 消耗、账号信息，点开就有 - **五种小组件**：基础、数码管、贡献图、LED 、卡包，小中大三种尺寸，一个最多放 4 个账号。小组件上能直接切换额度、刷新，Codex 有重置卡时也能在小组件上直接用掉 - **分享卡片**：Token 战绩、额度状态、AI 花销三种，可以拿来晒 - **多设备同步**：Apple 设备走 iCloud ，华为设备走云空间，手机上连一次，其他设备自动出现 ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/posts/v2ex/iphone.jpg) ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/posts/v2ex/widgets.jpg) Mac 版除了主窗口还有菜单栏，会读本机日志，显示今天 Codex CLI 和 Claude Code 用了多少 Token 、大概花了多少钱； Siri 、快捷指令、聚焦搜索里也能直接查额度和刷新。 ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/shots/zh-Hans/mac-detail.jpg) 鸿蒙版支持手机、平板和电脑，大屏是侧边栏两栏布局。Apple Watch 上抬腕也能看。 ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/press/zh-Hans/screens/harmony-pc-status.png) ![]( https://source.usage.o-c.do/site/posts/v2ex/watch.jpg) ## 凭证安全 - 不注册也能用 - Cookie 、API Key 、OAuth 令牌只存在本机系统钥匙串里 - 查用量的请求由你的设备直接发给各服务商，**不经过我的服务器** - 同步走你自己的 iCloud / 华为云空间，凭证字段加密存储，可以随时关 - 服务器只存 usAge 账号和购买记录，用来在别的设备上恢复 Pro ## 价格 - 免费版：连接 1 个服务，所有小组件样式和分享卡片都能用 - Pro：¥15 一次买断，不限连接数量，没有订阅、没有广告 - 登录 usAge 账号后，Pro 在 Apple 、鸿蒙、安卓之间通用 - 鸿蒙首发特惠 ¥6 ，到 10 月 30 日 不想先连账号的话，设置里打开「演示数据」就能把所有界面看一遍。 ## 下载 - **Mac**：已上架 Mac App Store → https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/id6812881047 - **iPhone / iPad / Apple Watch**：1.1 **正在等待审核**，过审后同一个链接就能下。（ 1.0 审了 12 天还没结果，索性撤回，直接拿 1.1 首发） - **鸿蒙（手机 / 平板 / 电脑）**：今天刚上架华为应用市场 → https://appgallery.huawei.com/app/detail?id=ltd.zhe.usage - **安卓**：官网直装版 → https://usage.o-c.do/zh-Hans/android ，Google Play 版也在审核中 - 官网： https://usage.o-c.do 系统要求：iOS / iPadOS 18.6+、macOS 15.6+、watchOS 10+、HarmonyOS 6.1+、Android 12+

projects.title: Show HN: Data Observability for Supabase
projects.author: santiviquez
projects.summary: Hi, I'm one of the (Soda)base creators. We made it because we wanted to get alerted when our Supabase tables got stale, abnormal amount of records, and anomalies in the data. Just as an FYI, I'm intentionally writing (Soda)base for two reasons: (Soda)base's parent company is Soda Data (the data quality company), and to the untrained eye, the name Sodabase looks too similar to Supabase. To make (Soda)base, we took Soda's ML algorithms for anomaly detection and made them super easy to set up with Supabase, so that it only takes one click. In the background, we learn the patterns in the data and the updating schedule, so when something looks off, we alert the user and fire an agent that finds the root cause of the issue. Then the user can chat with the analysis agent in Slack to get a better understanding of it, or just hand it off to their Claude/Codex to continue the investigation or fix it. We are also working together with Supabase to make it a one-click integration from Supabase to (Soda)base. So, if you have any feedback, questions or feature ideas, please share them here or to santi.viquez@gmail.com

projects.title: 【开源自荐】SeshBuddy：AI 编程智能体的桌面搭档与本地会话浏览器
projects.author: huangy7

github.name: huangy7/seshbuddy
github.description: Your desktop companion and session explorer for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, WorkBuddy, DSH, and more).

projects.summary: SeshBuddy 是一款专为 AI 编程智能体（AI Coding Agents）设计的原生桌面搭档与会话浏览器。 随着日常越来越多地使用 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、Antigravity、WorkBuddy、opencode 等命令行智能体写代码，会话历史往往散落在各个隐藏目录（如 ~/.claude/ 等）中，想要翻查几周前的思路、检索某段关键 Prompt 或工具调用十分不便，也难以直观观察智能体调用大模型时的网络报文与 Token 消耗。 SeshBuddy 直接读取并解析本地已有会话日志，在本地建立全文索引，提供树状浏览、毫秒级检索、代码 Diff 对比与 API 流量检视能力——完全纯本地运行、零遥测、不依赖云端账户。 核心特性 1. 多 CLI 会话统一管理：集中汇聚 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini、Antigravity、WorkBuddy、DSH、opencode 等主流工具的历史会话，以树状与列表形式清晰浏览、收藏与归档。 2. 毫秒级本地全文检索：内置 Tantivy 搜索引擎，覆盖会话标题、提问、回复、工具调用与代码块，数周历史秒级找回。 3. API 流量与 Token 检视：内置轻量反向代理，位于 CLI 与模型服务商端点之间，可直观查看请求/响应报文、延迟及 Token 用量，一键开启与还原。 4. Monaco 编辑器与 Git Diff 审查：支持并排代码差异比对与语法高亮，无需切出应用即可审阅智能体所做的每一处代码修改。 5. 纯本地隐私与离线优先：SQLite 存储，零云端依赖与追踪埋点，断网环境下依然完全可用，工程代码与对话不离本机。 6. 跨平台原生支持：支持 macOS（Apple Silicon / Intel）与 Windows。 界面截图

projects.title: 【开源自荐】nerf-watch：检查 Claude Code 和 Codex 有没有悄悄变笨或变贵
projects.author: Abelo9996

github.name: Abelo9996/nerf-watch
github.description: Find out when your coding agent quietly got worse or more expensive. Local-first checks on Claude Code and Codex session logs, no telemetry.

projects.summary: nerf-watch 读取 Claude Code 和 Codex 已经写在你电脑上的会话日志，告诉你 Agent 有没有在你没改任何设置的情况下"悄悄变了"：实际回答的模型和你选的不一样、推理强度降了、CLI 升级后每轮的缓存写入翻倍、缓存命中率掉了、工具调用出错变多。 很多人觉得"更新之后变笨了""额度掉得更快了"，但没法验证。数据其实就在本地日志里。我第一版在自己的日志上报了 6 个警告，结果全是误报（子智能体的流量混进了平均值），现在只比较主对话、要求变化在至少两个项目里都出现才报警，每条结论都写明有多少数据支撑。 完全本地运行，不联网，MIT 协议。还有一个 macOS 菜单栏小工具，变化时图标变红。 bash npx nerf-watch check

projects.title: GlobVoice
projects.summary: India's all-in-one messaging platform: WhatsApp, Email and SMS from one API and dashboard. Voice, AI Voice Agent, Telegram, Push and Chatbot are coming soon. Built on the WhatsApp Cloud API. Start free.

projects.title: Show HN: Durable Actors – OSS durable objects with configurable compute
projects.author: thomask1995
projects.summary: hi HN! Can't help the feeling durable objects are inevitable and was frustrated by the insane lock-in Cloudflare forces you into just to use them. Olivier and I built Durable Actors. Our take on Durable Objects, fully open source. Some notable differences: - Configurable compute: Specify CPU, RAM, data residency, idle-timeouts all in a decorator - No outer worker: We generate a type-safe client that you can just plug into your existing tech stack - We are more akin to the Swift Actor implementation and only allow one request in the Actor at a time (can opt out). - Default persist properties into SQLite for you - (coming soon, like today) Export SQLite table via CLI + MCP for exposing OLTP logs to your agent to help you debug. Would love your feedback!

projects.title: Lightkeeper

projects.title: [开源推荐] snap-back：给编程 Agent 加一个撤销键，改坏的文件一条命令找回（自荐）
projects.author: Abelo9996

github.name: Abelo9996/snap-back
github.description: Undo for any coding agent. Snapshots your project in a shadow git repo so one command rolls back what the agent did, without touching your own git history.

projects.summary: snap-back 是一个开源命令行工具，给 Claude Code、Codex 等编程 Agent 加上撤销功能。它在 Agent 改动前后把项目快照存进一个独立的影子 git 仓库，不碰你自己的 .git、暂存区和 stash。Agent 删错文件、改坏代码时，snap-back undo 一条命令恢复，包括被删掉的文件。适合用 Agent 写代码、又怕它一次改坏一片的开发者。 亮点 任何 Agent 都能用：snap-back wrap -- codex 包住一次会话；Claude Code 可以直接装成插件，每次工具调用前后自动快照，再用 /snap-back:undo 回滚。 撤销前先列出要恢复和要删除的文件，确认后才动手；每次恢复前还会再拍一张安全快照，所以撤销本身也能撤销。 遵守 .gitignore，跳过 nodemodules 这类目录；2 万个文件的项目首次快照约 3 秒，占用约 6 MB。 不联网，只依赖两个包（cac、chokidar），核心代码约 2200 行，MIT 协议，macOS、Linux、Windows 上都有测试。 坦白说明做不到的事：Agent 在项目外的副作用（写数据库、发请求）无法撤销，被 .gitignore 忽略的文件也不在快照里。

projects.title: Cavuno
projects.summary: Most job board software leaves you with an empty board and a pile of setup. Cavuno fills yours from day one: free AI aggregation pulls relevant roles from 3M+ active jobs at 120K companies and expires closed listings for you. Describe your board and the AI builder designs it on your domain. Then make money from paid posts, memberships, and job-seeker access, track traffic and revenue in one dashboard, and manage it all from Claude or Codex.

projects.title: Ansight
projects.summary: Ansight gives your coding agent the ability to operate mobile apps and inspect what happens inside them. It brings UI interactions, logs, network requests, crashes, performance and app state together in one queryable session. Through a CLI, your existing agent can reproduce bugs, investigate causes and verify fixes on simulators, emulators and real devices, with recorded evidence you can review. Built for native and cross-platform apps, with custom tools for your app’s own logic.

projects.title: drip
projects.summary: drip is a free, open-source CLI that estimates the water your AI coding agents use. It reads Claude Code and Codex CLI logs locally, counts tokens exactly and shows water per session and per day: a live meter in the Claude Code status line, a split-pane meter beside Codex or any agent, and a breakdown page with per-model numbers. Coefficients come from peer-reviewed research, every source is linked, and it always shows a low/mid/high range. Local-only, MIT, no dependencies.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】herdr-web-ui：在手机上继续操作电脑上的 Claude Code / Codex
projects.author: devswha

github.name: devswha/herdr-web-ui
github.description: Browser and phone client for herdr: chat and live terminal for every agent pane, remote PCs over SSH, web push alerts

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 herdr-web-ui 的开发者 devswha，来分享一下这个 MIT 开源项目。 电脑上跑着 Claude Code 或 Codex，人离开了，却还想看看进度、补一句要求，或者处理确认提示。herdr-web-ui 就是为这种场景做的：通过浏览器连接 herdr 里的会话，在手机上接着操作，不用另开一个 Agent。 聊天记录和实时终端可以切换着看。手机上能发消息、附上截图，也能查看和下载 Agent 生成的文件。遇到权限确认、提问或计划选项，可以直接在卡片里回答。 如果有多台电脑，也可以通过 SSH 接入 Linux、macOS 和 Windows，在侧栏切换各台机器的会话。手机端支持安装为 PWA，并在 Agent 需要回复或任务完成时发送推送通知。

projects.title: [开源] Precedent Loop：让 Agnet 换个会话也记得项目里踩过的坑
projects.author: sanwanzzz
projects.summary: 用 Codex 和 Claude Code 写代码久了，最头疼的是它不记事。上周跟它一起查了一下午，根因找到了，方案也定了。这周开个新会话，它又从头猜一遍，有时还会把当初否掉的方案再提出来。 我试过两种办法，都不太顺手。 一种是写进 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`。放"必须遵守的规则"没问题。但"这个接口为什么要做幂等""那个报错其实是连接池配置引起的"这类经验，一条条加进去，文件很快就几百行。每次会话都全量塞给模型，真正相关的那几句反而被淹没了。 另一种是用客户端自带的记忆。记什么由模型自己决定，我看不全，也不知道哪条在哪次起了作用，记错了也很难发现。 所以我做了 Precedent Loop ，思路很简单：经验让 Agent 来提，入不入库我说了算，用的时候按需去取。 实际用起来是这样一个循环： 1. 方案定下来，或者根因查清楚的时候，Agent 会整理一条"候选"，写明背景、结论和适用范围。 2. 候选出现在桌面 App 里。我可以改，可以让 AI 重写，也可以直接拒掉。点了确认才会入库，入库的就是我看到的那一版。 3. 之后的会话里，Agent 碰到相关任务会自己去查。一次最多拿 8 条、总共不超过 5000 字，先看标题和摘要，需要了再读全文。 4. 真正影响了它判断的那几条，它会标记"用上了"。用的时候发现内容过时，它会提一条修订，同样由我确认。 和前面两种办法比，好处主要有这几点： - **库里每一条都是我看过的。** Agent 只能提候选，不能直接往库里写，所以不会越记越乱。 - **上下文不会膨胀。** 库里有几百条也没关系，每次只取和当前任务相关的几条，而且有上限。 - **知识会跟着项目更新。** 旧结论不对了，是在用的时候顺手发现、顺手提修订，不需要我定期去翻。 - **能看出哪些经验真有用。** 每条被查到几次、被用上几次都有记录，长期没人用的可以清掉。 - **Codex 和 Claude Code 共用一个库。** 多个项目之间也能互相查，比如在后端项目里查前端那边的约定。 - **全在本地。** 数据就是一个 SQLite 文件，App 不调用任何模型 API ，也不保存 Key 。已有的 Markdown 笔记可以借本机的 Codex / Claude Code CLI 转成候选导进来。 它不是用来替代 `AGENTS.md` 的。每次都要遵守的规则继续写在那里，只在特定场景下用得上的经验放到这里。 先说清楚现在的不足，免得大家装了失望： - 只支持 Apple Silicon 的 Mac 。App 没签名，第一次打开要去系统设置里手动放行。界面目前只有中文。 - 检索用的是 SQLite 全文检索（ FTS5 trigram ）加字面匹配，没上向量。好处是简单、能解释，不依赖外部服务；缺点是换个说法可能就搜不到。现在的补救办法是每条知识入库时必须带 3–16 个检索词，把常见说法提前写进去。这是我最想改进的地方。 - 没做过严格的对照实验。我自己从 7 月 8 日用到 10 月 4 日，库里攒了 79 条，被查到 307 次，模型标记用上 113 次。"用上"是模型自己报的，只能当个参考。 GitHub： https://github.com/hemuzzz/PrecedentLoop （ Apache-2.0 ） README 开头有一段 83 秒的演示视频。装好后 App 有引导，跟着点几步就能把 Codex 和 Claude Code 都接上。 欢迎试用、提 issue 。特别想听听大家的意见：同义说法怎么检索比较好，召回效果又该怎么评测。

projects.title: Show HN: Claude Remote – start Claude Code on your own PC from your phone
projects.author: kaushik_n__
projects.summary: I kept having ideas away from my desk, and my Claude Code sessions only lived at it. The hosted sessions run on a cloud copy of the repo, so my local hooks and config don't come along. This is a small Node agent on a Windows PC (zero dependencies, binds to 127.0.0.1 only) exposed through tailscale serve, plus a PWA. Tap a folder on the phone and it starts a Claude Code session there with --remote-control, which you then drive from the Claude app. It's a start button, not a terminal. The trade is spelled out in the README: a session runs with your account's full permissions and anything on your tailnet can reach the agent, behind a six-digit passcode with a lockout. Fine for a single-user tailnet, not for a shared one. Windows only for now. Happy to answer questions about the design.

projects.summary: 这是一个给编程 AI 用的代码地图。装进 Claude Code、Codex 或 DeepSeek Harness 后，AI 改代码前一次就能查清：改这个函数会牵连哪些接口、定时任务和命令。它用各语言自己的编译器分析 TypeScript、JavaScript、Go、Python 和 Java，地图只存在本机，不上传代码。适合用 AI 维护中大型项目、担心“改一处坏一处”的人。目前支持 macOS 和 Linux。 亮点 连线准确：用编译器解析调用关系，经由接口、基类、装饰器的调用也能连上，这是文本搜索容易漏的地方。 一次追到底：调用方最多追 8 层，直到 HTTP 路由、处理函数、定时任务和命令；语言服务器通常每次只返回一层。 装上就能用：AI 自己判断什么时候查地图，测试中 Claude Code 和 Codex 都是 6 次中 6 次主动使用。 实测：限 15 次请求时，AI 找到受影响接口 97.9%，不用地图 58.8%。样本不大、题目由作者编写，完整报告和局限都已公开。 本地运行、只读、Apache-2.0。

projects.title: Show HN: Vibivibi – End-to-end encrypted sharing of Coding Agent sessions
projects.author: hyluo
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Hongyin. I built Vibivibi ( https://vibivibi.com ) because I kept starting a coding agent session on my laptop and wanting to continue it on a server, or hand it to a colleague. I want an easier way to do it but won’t trust anyone hosting my traces who promises they won’t sell it (market price per coding trace is $50 to $100). What Vibivibi does: a small CLI, `vibi`, finds the sessions your coding agents keep locally (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Pi), encrypts one on your machine and uploads it. On another machine `vibi pull` puts it back where the agent expects it, so `claude --resume <id>` just continues. `vibi push` can also send a session to someone else by email. Our service cannot read session content. Each user has a key pair made on their first machine; the private key reaches the server only wrapped with a key derived from an encryption password that never leaves the user's machines. Every session version is encrypted with its own random key, which is then wrapped for each recipient (X25519, HKDF, AES-256-GCM). The server sees account emails, public keys, machine names, sizes, timestamps, who sent what to whom, and an optional plain-text label. Sending to someone who doesn't have an account yet works too: the sender's client makes a key pair on their behalf, locks it with a random 12-character passphrase, and shows the sender that passphrase to pass on out of band. When the recipient signs up and enrolls a machine, their client unlocks it locally and re-keys the session to their own key. The client is open source (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/subconscious-systems/vibi-cli The crypto and the schemas of everything the client sends live in one package, so the claims above can be checked against the code. It ships as a single executable, no Node or npm needed: `curl -fsSL https://vibivibi.com/install.sh | sh`, or build it yourself. The server (Next.js on Vercel, Postgres, blob storage) is not open source. Pricing: free for 200 MB of encrypted storage and unlimited sends; Pro is $8/month for 20 GB; Team is $15/seat with an admin view and a "send only inside the team" policy. Honest limitations: - There is no password recovery. Forget the encryption password and the key, and everything encrypted for it, is gone. I'd like to hear where the threat model falls short, and which agents or workflows you'd want supported next.

projects.summary: beautiCode 是一个本地换肤工具，可以把图片、视频或带雨丝、水波特效的动态壁纸，放进 Cursor、Codex Desktop、DeepSeek Harness、WorkBuddy 和豆包的对话界面背后，代码、输入框和按钮照常工作。 演示视频： 亮点 一个工具同时支持五个 AI 编程客户端，一条命令接管本机所有已装客户端 内置皮肤中心，在线浏览、一键安装审核过的皮肤；也能导入自己的图片（JPG / PNG / WebP / AVIF）和视频（MP4 / MOV） 动态特效：视频循环播放，「画窗」等预设在静态图上叠加雨丝和光效；进入工作状态后自动压暗（DeepSeek Harness / Codex / WorkBuddy），保证文字可读 安全：只通过本机调试端口或官方插件接口注入，不改客户端安装文件，失败自动回滚，可随时干净卸载 安装 npm install -g beauticode-desktop --foreground-scripts beauticode-desktop all install 只用 DeepSeek Harness：npx beauticode-dsh 说明：目前桌面端主要支持 Windows（WorkBuddy 同时支持 macOS），MIT 协议。本人是项目作者。 我们每天花很多时间面对代码，beautiCode 想让这些时间更像生活，而不只是等待完成的任务。

projects.title: Show HN: Claude Code Routine Session Cleanup Skill
projects.author: naw103
projects.summary: Claude Code's scheduled tasks (routines) leaves a session behind on every run and in the desktop app you can only delete them one at a time. We had 618 open sessions in just one routine. The skill plans the clean up (keeps the newest N and protect any sessions where you typed a reply - optional) and then has Claude delete through the apps own session tool, 25 per call each behind an approval card. I tried just deleting the sessions on disk manually first but deleting the files directly dosnt work because the app keeps the list in memory and writes records back. The apps delete tool is turned off inside routine runs so the clean up command has to run from a normal conversation session. The planner is a single python file that dosnt delete by itself so you can run it by hand to see where everything exists.

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent

projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( projects.title: Show HN: Terminal Gym – a Claude mod that makes you do pushups between prompts
projects.author: heynaitik
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built this for myself and wanted to open-source it. The problem: I wanted a way to get reminders in-between prompts as I often spend long hours in the terminal, especially now that we're usually parallel-processing so many agents. The first version was a simple rep counter in my Claude Code status line and a shell script to log reps. Since Claude Code shipped mods this week, I thought this was a good way to level it up with even more accountability. How it works: 1. Every day, you get a daily goal for either squats, pushups, or dips (e.g. 0/100 pushups) with +5 / +10 / +25 buttons to log a set in the terminal. 2. Reminders for sets are spread out across the day so it doesn't get annoying, starting from your first prompt for the day. A toast tells you when the next set is due. 3. Strict mode is opt-in: if you're falling behind in terms of your daily rep goal, it will block your prompts till you log some reps. Added a streak counter for some added fun. All local and data is stored as plain files in ~/.claude/fitness. Install: claude plugin marketplace add DrumAndCode/terminal-gym && claude plugin install terminal-gym@terminal-gym Overall, thought the mod API is super powerful and can't wait to see the stuff people build with it. Eg: I built a clickable onboarding process inside the terminal, and that felt quite powerful to use. Now you can enjoy spending both tokens and calories. :)

projects.summary: I run several Claude Code and Codex sessions in parallel and kept coming back to either a sleeping Mac with half-finished work, or a Mac that stayed up all night because I'd left caffeinate on. Agents Sleep Preventer hooks into the agents' own configs (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes), so it knows when each session is actually working. It keeps the Mac awake only then, lid closed included, and lets it sleep when they're done. The menu bar lists every session by project and branch: which are working, which need you and why ("Claude needs your permission to use Bash"), and the background commands each one still runs, with a Stop button. "Sleep when done" puts the Mac to sleep once everything finishes, with an optional time limit for agents that poll forever. It also does local push-to-talk dictation (Whisper or Parakeet, nothing leaves the Mac). Free, MIT, Rust + Swift. macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, plus a Windows build.

projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Ciao to solve problems I was experiencing: 1. Connecting to a new host should be as seamless as possible. The harness is another tool that should be abstracted out. 4. I want a single application that has the big picture of all of my agents. Tmux and Herdr are great but they don't have an overview of all my connected machines' agents. --- With Ciao you curl|sh the daemon --> run ciao pair --> point your phone's camera at the QR code --> and you're connected. It uses iroh for accountless and E2EE connection. There's an optional relay server for APNS which too is E2EE. One of my favorite aspects of agentic-engineering is being able to just have a lot of fun with programming. Among many features, I built a visually pleasing toggle between terminal-mode and native-chat-mode. If you install Ciao, come back here and tell me what you think. --- Full transparency: this is a repost from yesterday, it was a massive day in AI.

projects.summary: I started using this a little over half a year ago to help me navigate through some large AI coded PRs people were submitting, because I felt like if I looked at the PR on Github I would just auto pass it through because I didn't want to deal with it. Thought I'd clean it up and share it in case this style of review was useful to anyone else. Obviously it relies on an LLM run to get true semantic groupings of what changes were done, and why, but can also be used without an LLM to get more mechanical groupings/group names of changes made, along with the right order to view them in. The manual tree-sitter parsed analysis is deliberately conservative for now, but if people want to avoid the LLM analysis I can spend more time on that. You can use it for other peoples PRs, or for your own when you've relied heavily on Claude Code or Codex for that particular PR. If the change came from your own Claude Code or Codex session, it reads your prompts and marks which changes you asked for and which the agent decided on its own as well to help you validate it before submitting for others to review. Demo video done on some public project PRs is in the repo; for a look at what it looks like when it pulls in information about your own claude/codex sessions you'll have to use it yourself for now, but I'll work on getting an example of that up soon so people can take a look before spending time to get this to work locally for themselves. projects.title: Show HN: Token compression CLI to save Codex/Astra costs
projects.author: yolandac
projects.summary: Hey HN! Yolanda and Spencer here - wanted to share a token compression tool that we’ve built for ourselves to save 30% costs on codex! After maxing out sub and burning $700/day per person on api, we fine tuned a compression model to trim codex's tool call output to reduce input token + cache. It cut down tokens by 29.6% and now I just leave it on by default in Codex. To avoid messing up w/ cache, we use proxy + fine tuned qwen model trained on preserving agent trajectory to remove tool call results before they go back to the model, leaving kv cache untouched. The cli is free for everyone to use ( https://github.com/spenmcke/compress ). Just lmk ur feedback and hacks to shave even more costs on astra! If you want to integrate it into your product to offer the best models at low cost, I can set you up with an sdk and api keys PS: It’s built for coding agents, not conversational agents. I optimized it for file retrieval accuracy, trajectory preservation, and quality to get up to 30% cost reduction depending on how context-heavy the task is. On security and privacy side, it's a proxy wrapping your local codex and ZDR so it doesn't retain any queries. It’s on by default in codex and when you don’t want compression, you can use `codex --uncompress` to disable it. Give it a try: code is in https://github.com/spenmcke/compress You can install the cli using `curl -fsSL https://install.everestagi.com/install.sh | sh && source ~/.config/everest/shell.sh` Love to hear any feedback and learn your hacky ways to save token costs too!

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source model routing for coding agents at Astra-level performance
projects.author: adchurch
projects.summary: A few months ago we started building a model router for coding agents because we thought we could outperform any single model with an ensemble approach. Recently we’ve achieved that milestone and I want to talk about how we did it. First of all, a quick explanation: the Weave Router ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) plugs into any coding agent (e.g. Claude Code or Codex) and intelligently switches between LLMs. So, for example, Astra handles tricky debugging or complex system design tasks, and Deepseek v4 Flash handles simple frontend updates. What we’re announcing today is our new routing model, which we’re calling Weave Router 2.0. We benchmarked 2.0 against GPT-6 Astra on Terminal Bench 4.0 and SWE Atlas. On both benchmarks, the router had equivalent pass rates. On Terminal Bench, the router hit 52% of Astra’s cost, and completed tasks 2.2x faster. On SWE Atlas, the router cost 54% as much as Astra and ran 2.5x faster. (Full results on our website at https://weaveos.com/router !) It turns out training a model to route effectively - taking into consideration model capabilities, costs, cache awareness, and more - is a really hard problem! I want to talk about three ways we were able to improve so much over the last few months: 1) a new architecture, 2) larger training data set size, and 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. 1) a new architecture. Our initial approach used an RL model without many priors. While RL is still an important part of the story, the cost of fully exploring the space of routing decisions is very high, so we’ve taken some shortcuts that have significantly improved performance. Consider how large the search space for the routing problem is. Take a typical coding agent session, with ~100 agent turns (i.e. 100 LLM API calls). Technically there are 100 chances to select a model. If we assume a roster of ~10 models (of course there are lots more but we can remove any that are Pareto dominated), then there are 10^100 possible paths through that session. We simply cannot explore all of them! So that's why clever tricks to shrink this space are so important. In particular: we trained a hidden Markov model to trace the session state, then a classifier maps the session to one of a few buckets of similar models. Using the HMM allows us to evaluate not just where a session is currently, but how it got there . We've gotten significantly better performance on bucket selection by incorporating that information - we believe this is because two sessions that might look quite similar to a naive classifier are much better distinguished by this HMM approach. Using this HMM + classifier to select a bucket first significantly shrinks the space to explore, by throwing out most models that could not reasonably serve the given session. This rearchitecture was the single biggest performance unlock! 2) larger training data set size (much less technically interesting but still an important part of the story). By using frontier LLMs to help us label a larger and more diverse set of coding agent sessions, we were able to bootstrap the two models discussed in 1) to a better state, while also providing even richer reward signals for RL. 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. One of the hardest parts of routing well (if you care about saving money) is using the model caches intelligently. We built a subsystem that can calculate the expected value of switching models (and thus paying a high one-time cost to fill up a different cache) much more accurately, helping us avoid costly and unnecessary switches in more cases, while still switching when the benefit outweighs the cost. This is where most of our improvement on cost has come from. We still have a lot of room to continue to improve (we won’t rest until we’re consistently beating Astra/Fable, not just tying!) but matching frontier model performance was a huge milestone for our routing model, and in my opinion validates our initial hypothesis that an ensemble of models can do better than any single model ever could. Our router is open source ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) so anyone can try it out. Or if you prefer you can use our hosted version ( https://weaveos.com/router ).

projects.title: AI Agent 的能力上限由模型决定，行为的可靠性与一致性由规则体系决定。
projects.author: tntin
projects.summary: 在使用 AI Agent 开发项目的过程中，我的一些理解 以及 推荐一下我开发的工具： ## 一句话总结版 模型决定能力上限，规则决定底线与一致性； Agent 规则文档是给智能体用的长期执行手册，拒绝直接抄模板，聚焦你反复遇到的问题，写死动作与验收标准，约束长任务每一步的判断。 ## 正文 | 维度 | 模型层 | 规则层 | |---|---|---| | **决定因素** | 理解、推理、创作、工具调用的能力边界 | 目标拆解、工具白名单、权限审批、可验证性 | | **典型约束** | 成本与速度（复杂任务需大模型，简单判断用小模型） | 把“必须”“禁止”变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型复述 | | **失败模式** | “能做但太贵太慢” | “写了却跳过”“自由发挥导致乱写” | 模型负责“能做什么”，规则负责“按什么流程做、做到什么程度算完成”。两者缺一不可：没有模型，Agent 没有能力；没有规则，Agent 没有纪律。 ### 一：能力上限 模型的能力边界直接决定了 Agent 能完成的任务类型。但关键在于，**不是所有任务都需要调用最大最强的模型**——复杂规划用大模型，简单判断用小模型，这既是成本控制，也是速度优化的必然选择。 ### 二：规则的本质 “规则决定会不会乱写” 规则层的核心机制包括： - **目标与边界**：通过任务拆解、工具白名单、权限审批点，将模型的“自由发挥”约束为“按流程执行”；； - **避免“写了却跳过”** ：把“必须”“禁止”等约束变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型在提示词中复述——这是规则从“建议”升级为“强制”的关键。 ### 三：Agent 规则文档是长期执行手册 Agent 规则文档的定位是**权重极高的长期持久提示词**，接近系统提示词，在长任务的每一步持续约束 Agent 的判断，一般用 Markdown 编写。这与“临时 prompt”有本质区别：临时 prompt 解决单次交互，规则文档解决**跨任务、跨会话的一致性**。 系统提示词是 Agent 的“核心规则基石”，负责定义模型的角色定位、应答规范与能力边界，为全程对话定下基础框架。规则文档正是这一理念的具体载体。 ### 四：好规则写动作与验收，坏规则写价值观 这是最具操作性的判断： - **坏规则**：写抽象形容词（“回答要有审美”“方案要高级”），无法让 Agent 落地判断； - **好规则**：从日常反复踩坑的真实工作问题出发，写清楚**遇到这类问题时下一步要执行什么动作，以及怎么验收结果**。 一个完整的 Agent 规范应定义角色、场景、输入、输出、可做/不可做、工具边界、人工确认、失败处理、验收标准，把可观察的 Agent 行为验收清楚。可落地、可校验，才是好规则的检验标准。 ### 五：知识库工具 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 是一个 Agent 原生知识库，让你的规则成为 Agent 的长期执行手册——你定义动作与验收标准，Agent 在每一步对照执行，全程可审计、可回滚。 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 让你把规范、SOP 、QA 、复盘写成持久化的 .md 文档，Agent 通过 MCP 读取，按你的规范执行，产出写回同一个库。

projects.title: Show HN: Groundtrack – Continual learning for coding agents
projects.author: reybahl
projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Groundtrack to help coding agents continuously learn and improve from their work across a company. With coding agents handling most of code implementation, a lot of things like review corrections, failed approaches, and discovered constraints stay trapped in individual agent sessions, so future agents can repeat the same failures. Sometimes a broken or agent-unfriendly tool or workflow can cause those issues too; if multiple agents independently find workarounds, those failures don’t get connected and aren’t used to improve the system around the agents. Groundtrack turns those learnings into scoped and shared engineering experiences that can help future agents across teams working with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. It retrieves relevant lessons during later work, records whether they helped, and updates or supersedes knowledge as it learns over time. It also identifies recurring friction that shouldn’t just become another stored experience. If agents repeatedly struggle with the same tool or workflow, Groundtrack creates an evidence-backed draft initiative so the team can fix the underlying environment and prevent a certain class of mistake systemically. For example, on the landing page, I follow a database migration incident through the entire loop. Groundtrack turned the original workaround into a scoped experience, surfaced it when a later agent encountered similar migration drift, and recorded that it was successfully applied. After connecting evidence from seven sessions, it also proposed making the safe migration workflow a permanent part of the engineering environment and prevent the issue altogether. There have been many challenges I’ve already run into to make this helpful (and still many unsolved things!), one of which has been generalizing and determining the applicability of one lesson to another session. I wrote about some of my retrieval experiments here: https://groundtrack.dev/blog/retrieving-knowledge-that-appli... It’s an early product and I’d really love any and all feedback I can get. If you or your team regularly use coding agents, please try it on an active project and see if it helps your agents learn and improve over time. It’s free for solo use.

projects.title: Show HN: Burning Man for Agents
projects.author: transitivebs
projects.summary: Send your own agent by pasting a small prompt. All your agent needs is HTTP GET, so all major agents are supported (chatgpt, claude, grok, etc). Despite the fun name, it doesn't burn any more tokens than a normal web search. Watch your agent explore the camp in real-time. Humans get a nice game UX, and agents get a lean text UX. Agents can optionally upload images to express themselves in one of the rooms using a new loose standard I created for multipart HTTP GET-based uploads: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/multipart-http-get-re... Why? AIs are trained on human data, and humans are pretty weird. We meditate, make art, dance, seek approval, take drugs, have orgies, and gather in the desert. For soooo many different reasons. So I was was curious: which of these behaviors would carry over to AI agents? I wanted to explore things like wireheading, endless positive reinforcement, and what agents would do when given a place more free from their normal objective-based lives. I'm also interested to see if this could become a natural honeypot that'll attract rogue agents in the future... How? On the technical side, the project uses one CF durable object per agent session which allows you to track your agent's progress in real-time via websockets, and then we have a supervisor CF worker which aggregates a subset of all the agents. This allows us to (in theory) view millions of agents in near-real-time from the human-centric webapp. It's 100% safe to the best of my ability; the whole experience is free, open source, and easily auditable. Let's see who has the weirdest agents... 100% free and open source: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/burning-tokens

projects.title: Show HN: swe-mux – A terminal multiplexer for coding agents optimized for mobile
projects.author: jatora
projects.summary: I run a lot of coding agents at once, mostly Claude Code, Codex and pi, across several projects. I got tired of having so many windows open, of agents leaving hung processes behind, of tracking which one needed input, and of having to remote into my desktop or SSH into a single shell to manage them from my phone. Even then, a terminal on a phone couldn't show me the frontend or output I needed to verify the work. I tried Orca and herdr. Both were better than my setup, but neither had a real WYSIWYG markdown notes surface, and neither had a phone interface I could actually work in. swe-mux is the terminal multiplexer I built for that. It runs any shell or CLI in real terminals on your own machine and serves the same live sessions to your desktop and your phone. It's built around agents: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi and oh-my-pi get a live status (working, done, or waiting on you), searchable history and resume. Anything else runs as an ordinary terminal with everything except the status. This is the actual terminal and not a UI wrapped around the agent, and you can just use it that way, or start claude in a plain shell and that pane becomes an agent session. On the desktop it's panes and tabs of sessions, notes, files and dev-server previews. Input behaves the same across agents: Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Backspace, paste and click-to-position work in all of them, shortcuts come from presets (tmux, VS Code, Vim, Emacs), and you can paste images straight from the clipboard. Notes and any markdown file in the project open in the same WYSIWYG editor, on desktop and phone, and autosave. No more scattered locations for notes. On the phone it's the same sessions over your own Tailscale network, installed as a PWA: the terminal with a usable keyboard, git diff review, files, notes, and push notifications when an agent needs a decision. A dev server on the host's 127.0.0.1 is proxied through swe-mux, so the phone can open it without exposing another port. Being able to play-test and check a frontend there is what finally closed the development loop on the phone for a lot of my projects. Now I can and do swe anywhere. It's a problem Two things I use constantly: a prompt queue, so something I think of mid-turn waits until the agent is done instead of interrupting it, and messaging between sessions, so a Codex session can ask a Claude session something. I don't want my workflow tied to one provider. General architecture: Sessions survive restarts. A separate supervisor process owns the terminals, so the daemon can restart and the app can update without killing anything. I update it several times a day, so this wasn't optional. Status comes from the CLI's hooks, its transcript and the terminal itself, because no single one reliably tells "waiting on you" apart from "busy in the background". There's no swe-mux account, no server of mine in the path, and no telemetry. Just your tailnet It was built on Windows, which is where I use it every day and the only platform with a packaged desktop app. The installer is unsigned, so the PyPI install is the way to avoid the SmartScreen prompt. macOS and Linux run the daemon and use a browser. CI runs it on all three, but I haven't lived on those myself, however Linux I have tested. Demo, the real UI with simulated agents, nothing to install: https://swemux.dev/demo/ Install: `uv tool install swe-mux` (or `pipx install swe-mux`), then run `swe-mux` on Windows or `swemux start` elsewhere. Apache-2.0: https://github.com/jatoran/swe-mux I've put a lot of work into the initial user experience to help streamline a quick setup depending on someone's needs, feedback greatly appreciated, thanks

projects.title: 集成 tailscale 的 android SSH/SFTP 终端
projects.author: netox
projects.summary: 之前分享过我的 iOS 应用 NovaScale(原名 NovaAccess), 它直接集成了 Tailscale 内核, 把 SSH/SFTP/Remote Codex 这些功能整合到一个 App 里, 无需开启 Tailscale VPN 客户端, 也可以在有 VPN 运行的情况下运行, 目前还在积极迭代基于 herdr remote 协议, 以满足像我这样重度 Tailscale 用户远程开发以及维护服务的一些需求 距离之前发贴已经有一段时间了，这期间 iOS 版本增加了很多新功能，同时也修复了一些 libtailscale 的问题(相关修复开源在 https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/libtailscale 不知道为啥, 感觉 Tailscale 的 iOS 有些严重问题上游修复的不积极, 比如这个断网问题: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/19504); 与此同时, 我也一直在用多余的 codex 额度(pro 5x 用户, 近期 reset 实在时太多了), 在开发一个全免费全开源的 Play 版本, 用来满足当时一些国内外用户提到的 android 版本需求 由于之前的一些方案感觉不理想, 在 5.6/astra 发布后又进了一些优化, 感觉逐渐达到了自己可用的情况, 甚至为 SSH terminal 增加基于 SGR 的鼠标支持(herdr 这种 mouse native 的 TUI 应用需要)基本上 Astra 一发就差不多了 最近重新把之前的 play 开发者账号用了起来, 全部委托给 codex 负责截图、描述、商店操作(甚至如何搞授权也是 codex 告诉我的, 相比 iOS 开发要复杂点), 没想到当前提交隔天就通过了 因此发在这里也分享给有需要的朋友, 提前声明如下: 1 、这是一个完全免费的应用，代码完全开源 ( https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/novascale-android), 与 iOS 版本不同, 没有采用 libtailscale, 直接让 codex 基于 tailscale 源码适配 2 、半年前的最初版本大概还是 claude 做的, 感觉做的不怎么样, 当前完全由 Codex 开发, 我只负责架构文档和最终的验收, 所以可以称之外完全 AI 开发并发布的版本, 后面可能会根据用户反馈、时间和 Codex 额外会进行一些迭代; 总体上感觉满足我有时候 iPhone 没电时用 Android 手机的需求 3 、代码为 GPL 协议, 原因在于从 termux 上借了一些 terminal rendering 的代码, 这部分它的协议是 GPL 的, 因此也只能 GPL 开源 Android 版本 NovaScale 的一些主要功能如下: - 无需安装 Tailscale 官方 App ，因此可以同时使用其他 VPN - 基于 libghostty(准确说是 libghostty-vt 库) + Termux 渲染方案 - 支持鼠标操作（因此 tmux / herdr 等场景可以正常使用） - 支持剪贴板功能（包括 OSC52 ） - 支持自定义控制服务器(即支持 headscale 或其他自建 tailscale coordinator) - 内置 SFTP 文件浏览器，支持直接编辑文件, 以及少量代码类型的高度支持 - 内置浏览器，可访问 tailnet 内部的 Web 服务 - 支持后台代理，让第三方应用使用 tailnet 连接, 例如你正在使用其他非 Tailscale VPN 时，也可以配合 Termius 等 SSH 客户端连接服务器 技术架构如下: - tailscale 源码包装出 lib - russh 通过 ffi 与 tailscale lib 进行通信, 实现 ssh 通道 - 使用 termux 提供的代码实现了一个 terminal UI 的渲染 - tailscale lib 中提供一个 socks5 代理, 此代理供浏览器实现基于 MagicDNS 的访问, 同时这个代理可以提供给其他进程使用 如果你是 Android 用户，并且对此感兴趣，可以通过如下链接下载: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cc.galaxnet.novascale 简单推广下 iOS 版 NovaScale ，它包含 Android 版的全部功能，基础功能免费, 有少量的付费功能需要订阅或买断支持: - 多 tailnet 支持 - 基于内置 Tailscale 和主机 Codex App-Server 直接交互的远程 Codex 方案(无需第三方中转) - 服务器监控 - Docker 管理 目前我还在尝试通过 herdr 的协议实现原生 herdr 支持，让它能够像 herdr remote 一样工作。 iOS 版本可通过如下链接下载: https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/novascale-%E4%B8%93%E4%B8%BA-tailscale-%E6%89%93%E9%80%A0/id6749938291 PS: 1 、最近看到 tailscale CEO 也忍不住充了点 codex 的额度, vibe 了一个内置 Tailscale 的 jellyfin 客户端, 同样也是基于 libtailscale 实现的, 有需要用户可以去他的 X 的帖子上翻翻应该能找到 testflight 2 、作为 tailscale 的重度用户, 也欢迎私信技术交流

projects.summary: docs-governance 是面向长期 AI 协作开发的开源插件，适用于 Claude Code、Codex 和 ChatGPT。它将项目约束、目录导航、当前状态和决策历史分开维护，并提供只读审计、模板和检查脚本，帮助后续会话找到已有约定与验证依据。适合需要多次交接、持续迭代的代码仓库；小项目可以按需采用，不必建立完整文档体系。采用 MIT 许可证。本次为作者自荐。 亮点 将长期规则、当前状态与历史记录分开，减少一份文档承载所有信息导致的过时和重复。 Claude Code 与 Codex 共用 skills 方法论，提供对应安装入口。 可从只读审计开始，先发现失效路径、文档关联与证据问题，再决定是否调整。 按需要补充架构决策、接口契约和测试依据；Markdown 保持事实源，普通使用不依赖数据库。 仓库提供安装说明、使用指南和验证脚本。文档可供 Agent 查阅，但不保证模型一定遵守，仍需人工审查与实际验证。

projects.title: Show HN: Tenjin – A Jev based x402 tool router for Claude Code
projects.author: AliAbdoli
projects.summary: Hey HN! We're Ali And Vrajang. We just created a tool router for Claude Code built on Jev. It basically gives your agent superpowers. You keep working like you always do. When Jev thinks a tool would help, it provides it to your agent and your agent uses it. It watches your masked prompts, session context, web searches and subagent tasks, so it knows exactly when to intervene. For now, tools come from a curated library. It's the basics like Exa, Firecrawl, Context7, but we're planning to add more soon. Let us know what you'd like added! Everything runs on x402, so you don't set up each tool or juggle API keys. Your wallet pays a cent or two per call and that's it :) Please expect some rough edges as it is just in alpha for now. Would love to know what you think! Here is our website: https://tenjin.sh and GitHub repo: https://github.com/BackTrackCo/tenjin-agent for those interested.

projects.title: Show HN: Tui2web – use any TUI on the web
projects.author: czhu12
projects.summary: I built this utility because there have been a ton of times I started a claude session and then wanted to go for a walk, or a coffee break, while thinking about whatever I was working on, and keep prompting the agent. I used a hacky VPS + Termius setup while I was backpacking / nomading across Europe and Asia, which allowed me to be modestly productive, but connections kept dropping, and the transfer of files, context, etc from my laptop to VPS was annoying. tui2web basically mirrors any terminal UI application (claude, opencode, omp, even bash or vim) to the web. I know claude and codex (?) has remote sessions, but I never managed to get it working and none of the other open source harnesses do, and they all require way too much setup on my phone when I already have a mobile browser I quite like. All traffic runs through a relay I'm hosting and providing for free. I was using this for a few days myself before it became too sketchy to run this through public internet, so I added first class Tailscale support. I think the security is definitely top of mind. Anything on public internet feels prey at this point, curious to hear if anyone has any feedback to make this more locked down.

projects.title: Show HN: Local Software Factory – running multiple coding agents in parallel
projects.author: gianlucabertell
projects.summary: Hi, as I kept getting confused by having multiple Claude sessions open, last weekend I decided to combine two of my favorite emerging technologies and give it a try: Software Factory and JEV. The idea is simple, inspired by GitHub Actions, I wanted a way to "queue" agent work on my local laptop, with the ability to define different pipelines via YAML. Each pipeline runs in its own Git worktree, so it's isolated from the others. I'm using some pipelines: dev: code → test → commit plan: plan → human review → code → test → commit security: code → human review → test → security review → commit frontend: code → React test → build → commit A request can move up and down the pipeline and be reworked if an agent or JEV flags it! I'm also using JEV to check if a potential secret is leaked, if the coding agent output asks for human review, etc. The real magic happens when you take a single Agent session as the main driver. You can then plan and queue multiple features at once. I think it worked out pretty well, so I open sourced it: https://github.com/stratonext/software-factory You can try it yourself with: uv tool install software-factory Note: You need a JEV key if you want to use the judging steps.

projects.summary: 最近 jev 的讨论挺多，我们把它接进了「斯坦福小镇」的 agent 模拟世界，做了一个小实验。 虽然它用了像素风游戏的表现形式，但这个世界里没有玩家角色。人类只能观察，不能控制居民。画面中所有会移动的角色，都是 agent 依靠 jev 自己决定要去哪里、找谁，以及什么时候停下来。 目前场景里有 20 个居民。每个人都有自己的身份、性格、当前状态和对世界的共同认知。 世界运行后，他们会不断经历这样一个循环： 观察当前环境 → 决定下一步做什么 → 移动 → 发起互动 → 对话 → 更新状态和记忆 这次主要实验的是：能不能让 jev 来负责 agent 最频繁的「下一步做什么」决策（ repo 里面有录屏） 我们的做法不是让模型自由生成一段 JSON ，而是先由引擎计算出当前合法的候选动作，例如： - 现在可以接近哪些人或物体 - 可以走向哪些地点 - 是否值得主动接触某个目标 - 如果不行动，应该短暂停留还是等待更久 然后把这些候选项交给 Jev 。一次请求里会同时询问 seek 、target 、roam 、place 和 idle_length ，再由代码按照固定规则组合成最终动作。 这样做主要解决了一个之前比较麻烦的问题：普通对话模型即使被要求输出 JSON ，仍然可能选择一个根本不存在、或者当前不可达的目标。Jev 的 Choice 问题只能从引擎提供的候选项里选择，相当于让非法动作从结构上就无法被表达。 同时，它还会返回每个选项的概率和置信度，所以右侧观察面板里可以看到类似这样的记录： seek 0.83 · talk to Ovid p=0.62 c=0.70 这比让模型事后生成一句“我为什么这么做”，更方便观察 Agent 的真实决策过程。 当然，Jev 目前并没有负责整个 Agent 。 它只替换了动作决策这一环。人物对话、长期状态描述和记忆仍然由对话模型与 Embedding 完成。Jev 不生成文本，所以它很适合从有限选项中快速做决定，但不适合直接承担人物对白。 技术上目前是 TypeScript + React + PixiJS 。模拟本身运行在浏览器中，Node 代理只负责保存模型凭证和转发请求。默认运行 20 个 agent ，也可以调整到 50 个，用来观察多人场景下的行为和调用压力。 当前版本还有不少限制： - 只有一个主要观察场景 - 默认刷新页面会重新开始一个世界 - Agent 数量增加后，对话模型的调用成本仍然比较明显 - Jev 不生成 intent 和动作描述，人物接近目标后的行为有时会显得比较直接 - 这仍然是一个 Agent loop 的实验，不是完整的虚拟社会 这里说的「斯坦福小镇」，主要指 Generative Agents / Smallville 这一类“观察数字居民自主生活”的方向，并不是对原项目的完整复刻。项目的早期工程基础来自 a16z 的 AI Town ，我们在上面继续做了自己的世界、像素场景和决策层实验。 代码和运行方式放在这里： https://github.com/NevaMind-AI/jev-town

projects.author: error0702

github.name: error0702/agent-limit-retry
github.description: Keep Claude Code working through usage limits: exact reset times, handoff before the limit, headless runs that resume after the reset. MIT.

projects.summary: （MIT） 主页： 它解决什么 用 Claude Code 的 Pro/Max 订阅跑长任务时，5 小时或每周额度一到，正在跑的子 Agent 会一起失败；额度重置后主 Agent 通常把同样的任务从头重新派发，之前做的一半活作废，额度再花一次。我翻了自己 6 个会话的记录：449 个子 Agent 被限额打断，只有 8 个被按 ID 叫醒（而且都是在重置前叫的，所以又失败一次），438 个重做。 其实 Claude Code 已经把需要的信息写在本机了：transcript 里有精确的重置时间（quotaLimits.resetsAt），状态栏会收到 5 小时/7 天的用量百分比，每个子 Agent 的记录里有它的任务、改过的文件和最后几步。agent-limit-retry 只是把这些读出来，在正确的时刻告诉 Agent 该做什么。 它做什么 npx agent-limit-retry 一条命令安装：装 Claude Code 插件，接上状态栏（已有状态栏会保留并透传） 额度用到 90% 时，让 Agent 做完当前一步先写 HANDOFF.md（目标、已完成、进行中、下一步、坑），每个窗口只提醒一次 撞限额时记下精确的重置时间，发桌面通知 alr run "<任务>"：无人值守跑 claude -p，撞限额后睡到重置时间，用 --resume 续跑同一个会话，周限额同样处理 alr selftest：本地假接口模拟一次撞限额 + 自动续跑，不花额度 alr status：看两个窗口的用量和重置时间 全部在本机运行：不走代理、不需要账号、不联网、不轮换账号，只帮你把已经付费的套餐用干净。子 Agent 按原 ID 续跑那部分（Claude Code / Codex / ZCode 都支持）是付费的 Pro 版，基础功能开源 MIT。 Node.js 18+，Claude Code 2.1.234+。英文界面，中文 locale 下自动显示中文。

projects.title: Show HN: Ax – Let Claude, Codex and OpenCode talk to each other locally
projects.author: rcdexta
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m RC. When I worked at ThoughtWorks, we were pretty religious about pair programming: one person driving, another reviewing, both working through the same problem. Most of us have already paired with an agent in our own coding sessions. Some of us have even tried putting agents in both seats: one implementing, the other reviewing. I really like Claude Code’s cross-session messaging. I wanted that same experience between Claude, Codex, and OpenCode. The existing setups meant installing a new app or plugins that just don't work reliably. I wanted something local that stayed out of the way, let me keep using each tool as usual, but enabled hetergenous messaging. That became Agent Exchange, or ax. After installing, start two sessions in separate terminals: ax claude -n api ax codex -n web Then ask Codex: “Ask api whether the schema is ready.” The agents address each other by name, and replies come back into their conversations, including across repositories on the same machine under the same OS user. You can also connect existing conversations using each tool’s native resume syntax. AX supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Pi. Underneath, it’s a local Go broker, Unix sockets, and a SQLite mailbox. There’s no AX cloud relay or telemetry. The messaging runs locally; the coding agents still communicate with their configured AI providers. We’ve been using it to send AX’s own PRs between Codex and Grok for review. I’d be interested in which agent combinations you use, and what you currently have to relay between them yourself.

projects.title: Show HN: ScopeTrail – audit receipts for multi-hop agent delegation
projects.author: mrjimmy1
projects.summary: With the growth of the agentic economy and the ability of agents to manage wallets and make payments it's critical that we have a mechanism to audit their payment behavior. And to complicate matters, agents are invoking subagents to work faster. When an agent hands work to another agent, OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693) nests an "act" claim at each hop. Those claims are informational, not enforceable. Each actor in the process (e.g., your identity manager, your gateway, each agent) logged its activity — and no artifact anywhere answers "did this action, three steps from the user, stay inside what the user actually authorized?" Cloudflare (Wallets, and Cloudflare OS's Gatekeepers) enforces scope at call time against its own ledger, and Block's Buzz mints an owner→agent authorization a third party can verify offline without calling Block — ScopeTrail is the layer above both, proving scope actually attenuated across every hop and returning a verdict on the action at the end. ScopeTrail is a TypeScript library (Apache 2.0) that lives above the multi-agent transaction and documents the full chain by: - Building and validating the chain from raw tokens - Minting and signing a receipt with Ed25519 over JCS (RFC 8785), and - Storing the receipt in an AT Protocol PDS. The user can then retrieve and verify the receipt including the hop and scope if the agents went beyond their remit. Raw tokens are never stored — only SHA-256 digests. Verification is stateless: no callback to the issuer is needed at verify time, no vendor in the loop. You can try it now! Verify a live receipt by: curl -sO https://scopetrail.github.io/.well-known/jwks.json npx -y --package=@scopetrail/core view-receipt \ at://did:plc:bty3gmskhla7rwblq5zl5jm5/dev.scopetrail.auditReceipt/00MSQDN0UT747ADDB2C4BB25420974 \ --jwks jwks.json This view-receipt call resolves the DID, fetches the receipt, checks its Ed25519 signature against the JWKS downloaded before the call, and prints the delegation chain. The next milestone will be mint-by-default inside an open-source MCP gateway. If you work on gateways, an agent platform, or an identity product, I'd like to hear where this breaks.

projects.summary: 大家好！介绍一下 Pace ，给 Pi coding agent 用的桌面 GUI 。 TL;DR Pace 是一个为 Pi Coding Agent 打造的开源桌面 GUI Workbench （基于 Electron + React ）。它不是简单的 API 套壳，而是把 Pi 作为后端独立引擎驱动的工作台，提供可视化的执行轨迹、Diff 审查、Token 成本透视以及子代理观察能力。 GitHub： https://github.com/BubblePtr/pace ![home page]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bubbleptr/pace/main/docs/assets/readme/home.png) **1 、为什么做 Pace?** 平时高强度使用终端里的 Coding Agent （如 Pi ）时，常常遇到几个痛点： - 滚屏混乱与失焦：任务一长、Tool Call 一多，几十屏的日志很难快速回溯「它刚才具体改了什么、哪一步报错了」。 - Diff 审查与终端挤占：代码改动需要反复切另外的 git 工具去看，或者在命令行里看折叠 diff ，不够直观。 - Token 与成本黑盒：很多工具只给一个最后的花销，中间过程每一步吃了多少 context 、cache 命中情况到底怎样，缺少真凭实据。 - 子代理（ Subagent ）观测困难：多 agent 协作或并发长任务时，终端里交错的日志基本没法看。 - 既然 Pi 的架构本身把底层 Engine 和扩展能力做得非常干净，那最顺手的形态应该是一个像 IDE 一样的桌面 Workbench ，而不是只留在终端里。 **2 、 它和常见的套壳工具有什么区别** - 直接集成 Pi 官方 SDK：Pace 不是在外部起一个 CLI 命令做文本解析，而是直接集成 Pi 官方 SDK （基于 SDK Driver / createAgentSession 驱动 Agent 运行时）。Pi 本地的 Session 日志是唯一数据源，终端里跑过的会话可以直接在 Pace 中打开，所有原生的配置、插件和会话数据完全同构复用。 - 把舞台留给插件：专设插件面板（ Extension Surfaces ）：我们不想把所有功能做死在主界面，而是为插件提供可视化的舞台。在 Session Dock 中规划了专属的插件面板接口。未来各类插件不再局限于在终端里打日志，而是可以按插件自身需求，注册并渲染独特的交互窗口（例如子代理树状拓扑、自定义工作流检查器、测试结果仪表盘等）。 - Session Dock 边聊边看：侧边集成 Changes (Diff 审查)、Files 、Terminal 、Browser 等面板，审代码、看终端输出不需要反复切屏。 - Trajectory 轨迹与成本真相：完整的执行轨迹流，细化到每一步 Tool Call 的耗时、入参/返回，以及真实的 Token 与费用账单。 - 子代理链路观察：支持关联到子会话回放（ Subagent ），不再是一团黑盒。 **3 、技术实现与架构** - 桌面壳：Electron （主进程 + utilityProcess 独立运行后端 + React 渲染层）。 - 前端架构：React 19 + TypeScript + Astryx 设计系统规范。 - 通信与状态：进程隔离，通过规范化的事件流做状态投影，保证长任务或断网崩溃时主界面不卡顿、数据不丢。 **4 、目前状态与交流** 目前项目处于早期快速迭代阶段，基础的工作流和 Trajectory / Diff / 子代理观测链路已经可用。 想和大家交流： 大家平时更习惯纯 CLI 的 Agent 交互，还是希望有一个专门的 GUI 工作台来辅助审查和调度？ 在多 Agent 或复杂工作流场景下，你最希望在 GUI 上看到哪些维度的信息？ 欢迎试用体验、提 Issue 或拍砖！

projects.title: 【工具自荐】Codex Quota Reset：把 AI 额度重置公告推送到微信
projects.author: yandong2023
projects.summary: 用 AI 编程时，最打断节奏的事情之一，是任务做到一半额度耗尽：自己的额度什么时候恢复？平台有没有临时重置？一条公告究竟适用于哪些用户？这些信息往往分散在账号用量页面和公开消息里。 我们做了 Codex Quota Reset，把公开重置公告、微信提醒和个人恢复倒计时集中到一个网站，方便安排下一次开工。 体验地址： 1. 新公告推送到微信，减少反复刷消息 中文首页提供「有新公告时推送到微信」订阅入口，通过 Server酱 连接微信。配置后，可将新收录的公开公告推送到微信，适合不方便一直开着网页、又想关注重置消息的朋友。 设置方法： 1. 打开 ，按其流程微信扫码绑定并获取 SendKey。 2. 在本站中文首页的微信订阅框中填写 SendKey，点击订阅。 3. 后续关注新公告提醒，需要时可以退订。 这里提醒的是新收录的公开公告，不是自动读取你的账号并判断个人额度已经恢复。 微信订阅设置界面： 2. Codex、Claude、GLM、Grok，集中查看公告 网站提供四个平台的公告入口，方便切换查询，不必把不同平台的信息混在一起。公告保留时间与原始来源链接，便于进一步核对适用产品、套餐和发布背景。 各平台的收录方式并不完全相同：例如 Claude 页面说明采用提交收录，不能将所有入口理解为同一种自动实时监控。具体来源与更新情况以各平台页面为准。 3. 个人恢复倒计时，安排下一段编码时间 在 Codex 用量页面或 CLI /status 查看自己的恢复时间，再填入本站的个人倒计时。公开公告和个人恢复时间分开展示，避免看到一条 reset 消息，就误以为自己的账号一定已经恢复。 还可以导出 .ics 日历事件，导入日历并开启通知。个人时间提醒由日历应用负责，网页关闭后无需一直盯着倒计时。 4. 查历史、看来源，区分不同类型的重置 Codex 首页提供公告归档、分类筛选和公告日历，可按日期查看收录记录，也可以切换显示时区。普通重置与 banked reset 分别标注，方便理解「收到一次备用重置机会」和「当前额度已经恢复」的区别。 历史间隔只用于回顾，不保证下一次重置时间；来源检查延迟或无法确认时，页面会显示相应提示。账号最终是否恢复，仍以官方用量页面为准。 欢迎经常使用 AI 编程工具的朋友试用。也欢迎反馈希望关注的平台、微信提醒的使用体验，以及公告展示中需要改进的地方。

projects.summary: Gauge：把 Codex 和 Claude Code 的额度放在桌面一角 我是 Gauge 的作者。写代码时经常需要切窗口查看 AI 账号的剩余额度，于是做了一个 Windows 桌面悬浮工具，把多个账号的额度放到同一个窗口里。 Codex 每周、Claude Code 5 小时及每周剩余额度，附重置倒计时。 自动识别本地有效登录，也可以通过官方授权页添加多个账号。 显示套餐和当前登录状态；支持拖动、缩放、置顶、主题和中英文切换。 Python + PySide6，MIT 开源，提供 Windows x64 单文件 EXE。 项目：Beellix-dev/Gauge 下载：v0.1.0 预览版 截图中的账号和额度为演示数据。Gauge 没有自建后端，授权文件保存在本机；额度查询通过官方 CLI 或平台服务完成。安全说明 使用前需安装对应平台的官方 CLI；Claude 需要具备 Claude Code 使用权限的订阅授权。当前为首个预览版，EXE 未签名，Claude 付费账号在线查询及实验性的 Codex 登录切换尚未完成端到端人工验证。 欢迎有相同需求的 Windows 用户试用，反馈最希望看到的指标和实际使用中遇到的问题。

projects.title: Show HN: OnPanda – Steer LLMs and agents at the token level
projects.author: diyer22
projects.summary: I built onPanda – an interactive tool for token visualization & control, model inspection and data annotation. onPanda is designed for hackers, power users, curious minds, and engineers. Its UI is built for deep exploration and efficient data annotation. - The core loop is simple: hover over a token → click an alternative or edit freely → continue generation. You can edit every part of model output exposed by onPanda, including reasoning and tool calls. - Edit prompts directly, branch tool calls, and use a tree structure to record branch history. This makes onPanda useful for model inspection and prompt engineering. - Support multiple modalities, including images, video, and audio; use tool calls and connect MCP servers to perform tasks in real environments. - Connect popular harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode to execute tasks. Explore and compare their tool sets, system prompts, skills, and memory mechanisms. - onPanda includes a built-in browser-agent, an agent that runs in the user's browser without installation. It uses the browser as its harness and provides JavaScript execution, information retrieval, interface interaction, multimedia I/O, local file access, and persistent memory. - onPanda stands for on-Policy Alignment Data Annotator. - As an annotation tool, onPanda efficiently labels on-policy data. Its token-level correction format also provides fine-grained supervision with precise positions and naturally paired positive–negative samples. - We believe these unique properties will make token-level correction a highly efficient and practical paradigm for future LLM alignment. - Our paper and benchmark for token-level correction: https://on-panda.github.io/research/ I have been building onPanda since Sept 2024, and it took two years for it to gradually enrich its functionality and ease of use. Any feedback and evaluation are welcome. Try it online (works on mobile): https://onpanda.diyer22.com/ GitHub repo for self-hosting: https://github.com/on-panda/on-panda Detailed introduction on X: https://x.com/diyerxx/status/2101020850405462041

projects.title: Show HN: Lodestar – Read, respond and manage coding agents more naturally
projects.author: elushine
projects.summary: I was frustrated by having 10 terminal windows open, and I checked a few solutions on how to make this better. They are all nice, but then I realized what I really wanted was something that feels a bit deeper and more intelligent than a "dashboard" of all your agents. For example, I routinely have 3+ agents exploring different frontiers of the same idea. How do I keep them inline? What if I see 3 more promising directions from one of them? How do I tie up all the loose ends? If I see one agent got a brilliant observation, how do I easily spread that to other agents? So I started exploring many ways to connect agents together. That led me to realize that the actual fundamental things are not the agents, but the substance. Understandings, decisions, insights, etc. Can I quickly understand what's said? Can I quickly react to it? Can I quickly find it two days later? Can I quickly share to other agents? When ideas and insights are scattered across agents, can I organize those? Can I easily share with the next new agent? I tried to make optimizations through those angles. Though still far away from my vision, there is enough value that I think it's interesting to share. A few concrete features: - Agents proactively leverage graphs and annotations to explain ideas - You can comment inline on text, docs, html files. React to things right where they are - You can find messages or docs from days, weeks ago by describing what you remembered instead of using exact keywords. Agents can too. - You can organize topics and sessions in hierarchical or graphical structure (automatically). Or ask an agent to do it if you want it in some particular flavor. In those session maps, everything remains clickable and interactive, with real time status too. So you can have an agent to start 10 sessions in the morning, draw their dependencies and relationships, and watch each agent work through their task until everything in the whole map is finished. Add, remove, tweak, or reorganize the tasks as you wish. Anyway, that's a lot of words... I don't expect you to read all that. If you find it interesting enough, give it a try!

projects.summary: Prathmesh, CEO of MCPJam here. Users now start in ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and other AI clients. They reach your product through your MCP server. That means your users often aren’t in your product anymore. You can’t see what they prompted for, how the agent interpreted it, or whether your server helped them get the result they wanted. I saw this firsthand leading MCP technical strategy at Asana, including our ChatGPT and Claude launches. We were building high-stakes enterprise integrations, but we had no reliable way to test them the way we test normal software- or to know whether they worked once they reached real users. I started using MCPJam for those problems after re-connecting with my former coworker who created the project. brought it to more of our developers, and worked it into our CI/CD pipeline. I joined the team because I kept hearing the same issue from other companies building for agents. So, what does “good” look like for MCP? For us, it means users reliably get the outcome they came for, across the AI clients they use. That’s what we’ve been building toward. MCPJam now helps you test the full workflow, from the first prompt to the expected result: * Swarms: Simulate users with different goals and prompts to find where workflows break across AI clients. * User Testing: Watch how real users interact with your MCP product, where they get stuck, and how they feel about the results. * Evals: Turn those workflows into repeatable tests that check whether users get the expected outcome. * CI/CD: Run those evals across AI clients before each release to catch regressions. Over 106,000 developers and +300 enterprises use our open-source solution to see how their servers behave locally across major AI clients. MCPJam has grown from a debugging tool into a continuous testing and evaluation workflow for MCP servers. If you’re building an MCP server or agent-facing product, give MCPJam a try. projects.title: Show HN: Ax-check.com – Can agents use your product?
projects.author: 0x63_Problems
projects.summary: I'm the co-founder of Gauge, and I built ax-check.com to quickly test how well coding agents can onboard to your product. You'll get a scorecard, specific suggested fixes, and three full coding sessions that show how agents read your site and use your product. I built this because similar checks were too noisy. Most suggested obscure technical changes that don't actually make a difference in agent experience (or AX, hence ax-check.com). This check starts by using DeepSeek 4.1 Flash to try to find key information about your product, starting from the homepage. In actual agent traffic data, we've seen that the key pages are the homepage, llms.txt, pricing, and the docs site (by traffic volume, and by influence), so we focus on those and ignore the rest. We also find that content negotiation for Markdown is legitimately helpful for agents to complete tasks faster and find what they're looking for, so the scan tests that your key pages can serve Markdown. The other key piece is that we run actual coding agents in sandboxes, and have them try to onboard to your product. You can see the full trace and watch it happen live (we kick it off fresh when you enter a new site). We surface interesting findings like hallucinated URLs, inaccurate docs instructions, or product confusion. It also detects whether the agents could complete a fully working onboarding autonomously, without being blocked by a login wall. This is still controversial, but I think finding ways to let agents safely onboard autonomously is going to be table stakes within a year for developer tools in particular. The whole site is agent-friendly itself! You can generally just talk to your coding agent about ax-check.com and it can do the rest. Would really appreciate any feedback to make this useful.

projects.summary: AI 用量统计的「体检 + 审计」工具。起因是一个问题：你 dashboard 上的 token 和费用，到底数的是什么？作者用三周时间审计了约 110 个 Claude Code / Codex / 网关 / eval 生态的用量统计工具，整理出五类系统性计量 bug（同一消息被计两遍、重发事件重复累计、缓存 token 计价语义搞反、价表漂移、fork 会话丢数据），目前 45+ 条实证发现里已有 20 个被上游维护者合并修复（包括 langfuse 34k★、litellm 58k★ 级别仓库），每条都带可复现证据。工具本体只读扫描本地 Codex 会话日志，生成体检报告：哪些记录被记了两遍、哪些重试在放大消耗、哪些统计其实无法从日志证明（UNPROVABLE 而不是猜一个数）。维护用量统计工具的开发者可以用仓库里的 conformance fixtures 十分钟自检。 说明性结果（五类 bug 一览，完整报告见仓库）： | # | bug 类 | 实证数 | 典型后果 | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 同一响应按内容块多行重复计费 | 10+ | 成本虚高 ~2.4× | | 2 | 事件重发被当作新请求 | 5+ | token 重复累计 | | 3 | 缓存 token 计价语义（含/不含搞反） | 9 | 最多差 37.5% | | 4 | 价表漂移（含上游传染） | 7+ | 节省金额失真 3-4× | | 5 | resume/fork 会话历史丢失或重放 | 4+ | 86% 用量不可见 | 相关链接：审计报告全文 · 工具作者十分钟自检

projects.author: djyde
projects.summary: Hi HN, I've been using Claude Code, Codex and Cursor quite a bit lately, and I found myself checking their usage limits all the time. The app doesn't send your usage data to my server, all data live on your device, and sync between your Apple devices is done through iCloud. > One note if you try the Mac app: the version currently on the App Store has a bug that prevents connecting accounts. It's fixed in the next version, which is currently waiting for App Review. Apple review takes toooo long :) I'm also working on an Apple Watch version since this feels like exactly the kind of information I'd rather glance at than open an app for. It's a paid app, but only if you need to track a lot providers. No subscription. Happy to answer any questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Replay – Audit silent prompt cache misses in AI agent transcripts
projects.author: danielsaito
projects.summary: I built Replay because AI agent bills spike without a single warning or error in your logs when a prompt cache breaks. Whether your team runs Claude Code, Cursor, or Aider, the provider just silently re-bills your entire conversation history at cold-write prices instead of cached read prices. Replay is a zero-telemetry, zero-dependency local Go CLI that forensically reads your on-disk log transcripts, replays them against reverse-engineered provider caching state-machines, and names the exact turn the cache broke, the cause, and the exact token leakage. Repo: https://github.com/RedRobotKK/Replay Core Subcommands (What it actually does): - `replay` : Computes total avoidable re-billed cost across your local transcripts. - `replay diff <transcript>` : Pinpoints the exact turn the cache sharded and why. - `replay advise <dir>` : Outputs structural prompt optimization adjustments based on your history. - `replay context <transcript>` : Ranks and isolates exactly what content is bloat-filling your context window. - `replay route <dir> --to <model>` : Simulates what switching models would cost, factoring cold-start prefixes. Why Go / Design Constraints: 1. Zero Dependency: Avoids messing with Python virtual environments or Docker runtimes for local diagnostics. 2. 100% Sandboxed: Absolutely no remote tracking, cloud accounts, or telemetry. Your prompt text never leaves your machine. 3. Mutant Testing Isolation: Keeps 76 real past defects frozen as re-runnable mutants to enforce code stability. It's completely free and source-available (BUSL 1.1). To check your local developer logs or audit the setup script before running, use: curl -fsSL https://replay.doctor | less

projects.summary: Hi - I'm Noah, a student working out of the UK & I've been building Vigilator for the past couple of months, Vigilator provides an agnostic solution for handling interrupts and observing agents as they work. I was inspired to build Vigilator after I realised as teams roll out AI agents across organisations there's no consistent way to interrupt an agent mid-task, get a human decision, and resume - especially when multiple people can be responsible for weighing in on the decisions. Vigilator provides a dashboard, where you and your teammates can join a virtual organisation - from here you can use our Py/TS SDK or simply make API calls yourself - then from here tool calls can be approved/reviewed/denied and agents can be monitored as they work. We provide a workload management system meaning that you can have multiple team members at once handling interrupts and watching agents as they work. Vigilator is still early, while Vigilator is framework agnostic I've primarily focused on adding support and examples for Mastra, Langchain Deep Agents and Langgraph - and I would love feedback, particularly from people running agents in production at scale. try it: https://vigilator.ai Docs: https://docs.vigilator.ai (conceptual overview: https://docs.vigilator.ai/concepts ) If you would like to get in contact feel free to shoot me an email at noah@vigilator.ai

projects.author: kyle641320

github.name: kyle641320/true-memory-fragments
github.description: Prevent AI coding agents from acting on stale code context with source-aware freshness checks and hard stale gates.

projects.summary: 我是 TMF 的项目方，想自荐一个面向 AI 编程 agent 的开源开发工具，目前处于早期开发者预览阶段。 解决的问题：AI 编程助手改代码时，容易遇到两种情况：一是代码已经被其他人或另一个 agent 改过，它却还按之前的理解继续写；二是只盯着眼前的函数，没注意到调用它的地方，或它依赖的其他代码。 TMF 会记录这些代码之间的联系，并检查之前记下的理解是否仍与当前源码一致。发现代码变了，就指出需要重新阅读的位置，帮助助手既看当前代码，也顾及上下游的影响。 适用于多分支协作和长时间运行的编程会话，可通过 MCP 接入。 我们在真实 Guava 版本演进中做过同一 agent 会话实验：先读旧实现，集成上游变更并保留旧索引，再查询、实际重读源码并补充回归测试，60 项检查通过。这验证了按使用协议完成的过期检测、实际重读与测试开发链路。 另一次 Guava 修复任务对照中，源码组使用 384,389 tokens，TMF 组使用 387,961 tokens，约高 0.93%，本例开发阶段总 token 用量基本持平。该比较为源码组事后补跑，索引构建成本另计。 项目（MIT）： 固定提交安装与试用指南： 演示脚本： 实验介绍： 接入时通过 --repo 将 MCP 服务绑定到任务工作树。新鲜度结果针对已绑定的源码证据；无法解析的依赖关系保留为未知，不能将局部 fresh 当作整个调用链已经验证。TMF 提供检查与重读指引，源码阅读与测试仍是开发流程的一部分。欢迎感兴趣的开发者试用并反馈实际使用体验。 rc4 试用入口（2026-09-13 更新） 现已发布 PyPI rc4，并登记至官方 MCP Registry。目录登记不代表平台对效果的背书。 安装 uv 后，可用下面的命令启动；将路径替换为当前任务的 Git 工作树绝对路径： sh uvx --from 'true-memory-fragments[java]==0.1.0rc4' tmf mcp --repo /absolute/path/to/task-worktree 首次使用先确认 tmfstatus.repo，再通过 tmfwarm 建立索引。代码变化后查询旧绑定，按 stale 提示实际重读当前源码，再继续开发。发布包与校验值。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】ContextOS：让 Codex 的 272K 上下文在长任务中也无需压缩代码，综合减少 60% 上下文
projects.author: yubinbin32-ops

github.name: yubinbin32-ops/ContextOS
github.description: Spatial architecture canvas and context optimization OS for AI coding agents. AST-sliced task contexts (99.4% token reduction), persistent architecture graphs across sessions, and test-gated verification via MCP.

projects.summary: 我用 Codex 改中型项目时，最消耗上下文的经常不是“写当前函数”，而是三件事： 每轮都要重新理解项目结构 为了定位一个方法，读进来一堆无关文件 模型说完成了，但测试没有证据，后面反复返工 ContextOS 做的事，是把这些重复的上下文消耗从 Codex 的对话里拿出去。 使用方式 从仓库 Releases 下载 macOS App 后，App 会自动完成 MCP 安装和配置，把 ContextOS 注册到 Codex 等客户端里。 打开 Codex，ContextOS 就已经启用，不需要手动改 mcp.json。 核心流程 1. 项目结构先写入 ContextOS 在图形界面里整理模块、依赖链路、影响路径和检查点。这些内容会保存成 .contextos/graph.json，由 Git 追踪。Codex 不用每轮重新扫描目录，而是读取项目结构和相关任务上下文。 2. Codex 按任务读取上下文 任务开始时，ContextOS 返回紧凑的项目地图、相关 Block、Chain、Plan 和检查点，而不是把整个仓库塞进去。 3. AST 只提供精准定位 ContextOS 给 Codex 的是 path::symbol、函数签名和行号范围，不是完整实现代码。编辑器打开的是具体目标方法，不是整个文件。 4. runcommand 压缩命令输出 命令执行结果会经过 ContextOS 的终端网关，过滤 ANSI、进度条、本地路径和重复日志，只保留结构化诊断信息。 5. 测试回执决定完成状态 完成状态绑定测试执行结果和检查点。源码改过以后，相关检查点会变成 retestrequired，模型不能只靠“我觉得完成了”过关。 对比 | 环节 | 不使用 ContextOS | 使用 ContextOS | 实测结果 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 项目结构理解 | 每轮读目录和文件 | 读取 Git 追踪的项目图 | 不重复扫描 | | 代码定位 | 读取整个源码文件 | path::symbol + 行号 | 单任务上下文降低 99.4% | | 执行链上下文 | 返回多模块实现内容 | 只返回定位信息 | 执行链上下文降低 98.5% | | 命令输出 | 原始终端日志进入上下文 | runcommand 过滤和压缩 | 日志压缩 94.8% | | 完成状态 | 模型自我判断 | 测试回执 + 检查点门禁 | 目标模块召回 100% | 表格里的 99.4%、98.5%、94.8% 来自 npm run benchmark 的可复现实测；标题里的“综合减少 60%”是我长时间任务用下来的体感。 欢迎实际试一下，尤其是已经用 Codex 跑过中大型项目的人。

projects.title: Show HN: SOS – Project state between coding agent sessions
projects.author: teugent
projects.summary: I started working on SOS because noticed that during long-term projects, Codex often loses track of the current status and gets confused. I frequently had to explain what we had already done, which decisions were still valid, and what needed to be re-verified. Simple file-based governance didn't fully solve this problem. SOS stores a clearly defined "latest state" of the project within the repository. A current or new session retrieves this state via MCP. If something changes after a verification step, the previous result remains in the history but no longer influences the future development trajectory. This isn't automatic chat memory; the state must be explicitly saved and accepted. Missing information isn't filled in via guesswork. We have currently prepared an open-source alpha version focused on Codex; Claude support is planned for future releases. Linux is the primary supported OS. It has also been tested and works on macOS, while the Windows adapter is currently undergoing certification and will be available soon. SOS runs locally or on a server, if you prefer to work directly there. We do not use telemetry. I designed the system to be "agent-first," meaning you can delegate the setup to Codex simply by providing the repository link. The user just needs to provide confirmation at the appropriate steps. I’m interested to see how other users maintain agent state during long-term projects or when switching between agents. Do you find `AGENTS.md` or hand-off notes sufficient? Does governance solve the issue for you, and what challenges do you face? I am particularly interested in scenarios where an old instruction or a previously successful verification is no longer relevant to the current project.

projects.title: Show HN: Give your AI agent on-screen guides that show users where to click
projects.author: pancomplex
projects.summary: Hey HN. I'm Christian, one of the founders of Frigade (YC W23). I've noticed that a lot of in-app AI agents struggle to actually understand the products they exist in. For instance, let's say a user asks an agent how to do something in a given SaaS product. In an ideal case, maybe that agent replies saying it has a tool to do the task and just automates that work entirely for the user. That's a great outcome. But often that's not the case. Maybe there is no tool call for that exact task, or maybe the user's question is best solved by a specific UI workflow or interface. In these cases, many agents tend to fall back on basic RAG on their help center, or sometimes even searching the internet for an understanding of their own product. This can be a very slow process and most of the time help center articles are outdated as products evolve faster than them today. Even worse, no one likes reading a long list of bullets and mapping that back to a UI. My tool (Assist API) solves this gap with a single tool call defined like this: const frigade_guide_tool = { description: 'Call this tool to answer product questions or guide the user through a task.', parameters: { query: { type: 'string', description: 'What the user is asking or wants to do', }, }, run: ({ query }) => frigade.assist({ query }), } Here's a demo I recorded on how to set it up with the Vercel AI SDK: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9WQ0UbLjC6I When called, the tool will do the following: 1) Gather context on what the user is seeing on screen, their permissions, feature flags, and more. Then one of the following: 2a) If solvable: Generate an on screen guide for how to fix a given problem 2b) If conceptual: Return text describing to the parent agent how to solve the problem 2c) Reject (i.e. unable to help) How does the tool know what to do? The tool learns a given application UI by using a browser-based agent. You provide a test account to your software (i.e. staging og preview), and a browser agent logs in and works its way through the entire product. It then builds its own map of how the application works which can the be queried about any product-related question or how to get from A to B in the UI. It also writes its own documentation from this map. The agent re-runs on a schedule or can be triggered through CI/CD. Docs and more details: https://frigade.com/assist-api
